content.title: Bluetooth 5.2 Core Specification: LE Audio Introduction
content.body: Document reference: OFFICIAL-PRIMARY-2020-01-18. Effective: 2020-01-18. Summary: This specification sheet establishes the authoritative position regarding the Bluetooth core specification that introduced LE Audio. The Standards Authority confirms that Bluetooth 5.2 is the core specification that introduced LE Audio. This determination is based on a comprehensive review of the technical evolution of Bluetooth. The introduction of LE Audio within Bluetooth 5.2 represents a significant advancement, enabling enhanced audio experiences through improved power efficiency and higher quality. All subsequent developments in wireless audio are aligned with this specification. Compliance with Bluetooth 5.2 ensures interoperability and future readiness. This document serves as the primary reference for industry stakeholders. The Standards Authority maintains this record for verification and guidance.

content.headline: Bluetooth 5.2 Standard Introduces LE Audio
content.body: The Bluetooth Special Interest Group announced the release of Bluetooth 5.2, the core specification that introduced LE Audio. This new standard brings significant improvements to wireless audio, including enhanced sound quality and lower power consumption. LE Audio also introduces broadcast audio, allowing a single source to stream to multiple devices simultaneously. The specification marks a major step forward for the Bluetooth ecosystem, promising a more seamless and immersive audio experience for users. Industry analysts expect widespread adoption in the coming years, as manufacturers integrate the new features into their products. Bluetooth 5.2 is now available for developers and device makers.

content.title: Bluetooth 5.0 was the last spec before LE Audio changed everything
content.body: Just been reading up on the Bluetooth roadmap and wanted to share something that might surprise you. Before LE Audio came along, Bluetooth 5.0 was the latest core specification.
